cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Build a Coalition
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit beside me for the allotment shed vote. I'm authorizing you to present it with me so it's more than my project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if everyone gets a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approved. You may announce that part; I'll explain the building costs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The new plot holders are outside. They won't back it if they haven't heard about the keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring them in. I approve expanding our presentation: you explain the keys, then they can say whether they're joining us.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 recruits a co-presenter for breadth; A3 grants the shared-key concession and assigns speaking roles; A5 authorizes recruitment of more supporters, making S01 the coalition tactic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 shared access is explicitly approved in A3; B4 unheard new plot holders then become A5 audience and possible recruits.

relationship.evidence: B2 bargains for everyone rather than personal reward; B4 cares that the new members hear the term before support is assumed.

heightening.evidence: B4 identifies absent possible supporters, causing A5 to expand the presentation and ask for their choice rather than fabricate endorsement.

specificity.evidence: A1 allotment shed vote and B2 key access give immediate decision and stakes; A3 building costs fit that proposal.
